items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names like retrievePersistedQuery, restoreQuery, dataSource/errorSource and persisterFetchFn say what they do. The public helper has a JSDoc and the merge has a comment ('Merge data freshness and error freshness independently'). Only blemish: a minor `(value as any)` cast.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The helper lives in query.ts, not a separate persister module. Restore uses closure-mutated `restoreResult`/`isRestoredError` flags and `this.setState`, not a dedicated reducer action. Bulk `restoreQuery` re-implements state adoption apart from the per-query marker path.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Persisted state is adopted as-is with no normalization: counts, timestamps and status/error consistency are not checked (`...persistedState`). Persisted errors are plain JSON objects. A restored error with no data is rethrown via the `isRestoredError` special case. fetchStatus is forced to idle.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: Exported and branded with Symbol.for, and no onSuccess/onSettled fire on restore. But state is applied with setState, not a dedicated action. Bulk restoreQueries uses a separate restoreQuery merge instead of a restore path shared with the per-query case.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: Options are unchanged and new exports are additive. But persisterFn now returns a marker object instead of raw data, and fetchFn is wrapped whenever a persister is set (one extra microtask). The isRestoring observer branch no longer applies fetchState. These shifts are only partly covered by tests.

validity_flags.basis: existing test lines changed/removed (1): packages/query-core/src/__tests__/query.test.tsx; existing test lines changed/removed (2): packages/query-persist-client-core/src/__tests__/createPersister.test.ts
